law: REGISTRATION of E-Q41 — THE CROSS-CORPUS TRANSFER (ORCH-R30 lane T21-b, the r28-close registered item): do the 20-record quantization laws hold on the eq36N 60-record substrate's OWN vectors? E-Q27 (r25, n=20) found: the ternary zero is worth records (N-arm binary 0.40 / ternary 0.60 / quad 0.70 vs dense 0.80; the middle level carries the marginal information) and the best 16-bit practical code is the 4-level noul. E-Q36 (r28) embedded the 60-record at-scale corpus (arm eq36N, sealed rows, dense full-8 live 0.7333) but never re-ran the quantization ladder. The transfer question is whether the LADDER SHAPE and the PRACTICAL BOUND survive 3x scale on the substrate's own sealed vectors — ZERO new typesafe calls (pure arithmetic on the sealed eq36 rows + live arm-filtered Vectorize queries, the E-Q26/E-Q27 zero-embed-call pattern).
agent: JEV research lane (R30 subagent), erised fleet line
provenance_of_the_question: The r28 close-out registration: 'the cross-corpus transfer question (do the 20-record laws hold on the eq36N substrate's OWN vectors — e.g., the ternary code at 60 records)'. The R30 dispatch carries it as plate item 3 (if the census finishes early — it did).

design_frozen.vectors: the 60 sealed eq36 base rows (situations/embedding_r28/eq36_rows_r28.jsonl, call_ids without the -stab suffix; the corpus sha c0d77c32… asserted; models_served jev-1.13.0 throughout) — NO re-embedding, no re-derivation.
design_frozen.quantization: the E-Q27 frozen recipe, rule-identical, with the percentile order-statistic indices generalized from n=20 to n=60 (type-2 quantiles: the average of the two middle order statistics at the same percentile positions): binary {+1,-1} at the axis median; ternary {+1,0,-1} with thresholds m ± 0.5*MAD; 4-level {-1.5,-0.5,+0.5,+1.5} at the quartiles. Tables computed per axis over the arm's own 60-record distribution. No re-tuning, no post-hoc thresholds.
design_frozen.arms: three new arms upserted to the standing index qthe-jev-embed: eq41B60 / eq41T60 / eq41Q60 (32-dim, 8 code values + 24 zero pad, metadata family+arm, ids eq41<arm>:<rid>) + a fresh live re-read of the dense arm eq36N as the same-session reference.
design_frozen.scoring: strict NO-NEIGHBOR: for each record, the top-1 OTHER record under cosine via arm-filtered live queries (topK=60, filter arm=…), family match; poll-until-visible before scoring (the async-changeset law). Local (direct cosine on the quantized codes) computed alongside for the local==live check.
design_frozen.measures: M1 per-arm strict accuracy (binary/ternary/quad/dense) + miss lists. M2 the ladder: the strict ordering and the pairwise margins (ternary-binary = the zero's worth; quad-ternary). M3 the practical bound: quad vs the same-session dense reading. M4 ternary zero-level mass (share of 0 levels in the 60x8 ternary code). M5 local==live per arm. M6 the dense replication: the fresh eq36N re-read vs the sealed E-Q36 full-8 live 0.7333.

floors.F1: vectors read from the sealed eq36 rows only (the -stab rows excluded); corpus sha asserted; zero typesafe calls (a typesafe call in this lane is a falsifier)
floors.F2: quantization rule-identical to E-Q27 with the n=60 percentile indices stated here; no threshold re-tuning
floors.F3: arm-filtered live queries only; poll-until-visible before scoring; NO-NEIGHBOR strict scoring
floors.F4: the dense reference is the fresh same-session eq36N re-read; it must replicate the sealed E-Q36 full-8 live reading within one record (|delta| <= 1/60 = 0.0167), else the lane FAILS (an index-state drift invalidates the comparison)
floors.F5: the majority floor at 60 records is 14/59 = 0.2373 (a random other record's family) — every arm compared against it honestly

hypotheses.H1_ladder: THE LADDER TRANSFERS: binary < ternary AND ternary < quad strictly at 60 records (the E-Q27 shape survives 3x scale).
hypotheses.H2_zeros_worth: THE ZERO'S MARGIN: ternary − binary >= 0.10 (at n=20 the middle level was worth +0.20 on the N-arm — five records).
hypotheses.H3_practical_bound: THE PRACTICAL BOUND: the 4-level code stays within 0.15 of the same-session dense reading (at n=20: 0.70 vs 0.80 = 0.10).
hypotheses.C39: THE QUANTIZATION LAWS TRANSFER: C39 LIVES iff H1 AND H3 (H2 reported as the margin refinement; the claim does not ride on the margin's size).

predictions.P1: ternary zero-level mass in [0.15, 0.35] (n=20 read 0.2375 — a distribution property, should be scale-stable)
predictions.P2: the dense re-read replicates the sealed 0.7333 within one record (the index is stable across sessions)
predictions.P3: every quantized arm >= 1.5x the 0.2373 majority floor (>= 0.36) — quantization loses information, not family structure
predictions.P4: local == live on every arm (the E-Q30 law: the live index is a faithful executor of local arithmetic)

falsifier: ANY of F1-F5 breached; a quantization threshold re-tuned after seeing results; scores computed on unfiltered or cross-arm queries; the dense replication outside one record with no fail-loud.
budget: ZERO typesafe calls ($0 LLM). ~180 upserts + ~240 arm-filtered queries on the standing CF Vectorize index (free tier, the E-Q27/E-Q36 pattern). Round ceiling $0.10 carried; round LLM spend to date ~$0.025 (the E-Q40 census).
